newsitem.title: INDIA: India reports progress in elimination of leprosy.
newsitem.headline: India reports progress in elimination of leprosy.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Friday that India had begun to show progress in its efforts to eliminate leprosy by the year 2000, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.

Deve Gowda told an international conference on the disease in New Delhi that India had already brought down the incidence rate of leprosy to one per 10,000 people in the northern states of Punjab and Haryana.

"Efforts are on to step up the programme (to fight leprosy) and bring down the disease incidence to this level in ten more states in the country by the end of next year, and we hope to achieve the same results in the rest of the country by 2000," PTI quoted Deve Gowda as saying.
Around 680,000 people, or 52 percent of the world's 1.26 million leprosy patients, are in India.
Up to 95 percent of Indians were resistant to leprosy and 80 percent of those affected by the disease did not carry an infection that could spread, Deve Gowda said.

Health ministers from 24 countries accounting for more than 93 percent of the world's leprosy patients are participating in the three-day World Health Organisation (WHO) conference that began on Friday.

Indian health authorities are carrying out a campaign to propagate the power of multi drug therapy, or MDT, to remote areas where people are not yet familiar with recent developments that help control or eliminate leprosy.
Leprosy is a skin disease that affects the mucous membrane and the nerves. If untreated, it can cause permanent damage to limbs and eyes.
